body:
hey there -

the error message describes the problem, which is that it's looking for a column expression, not text(), the latter of which describes a SQL statement.   For textual column expressions, use `literal_column()`, this is mentioned in the docs for case:

```py
from sqlalchemy import case
from sqlalchemy import func
from sqlalchemy import literal_column

colexpr = literal_column('asdf')
expr = case(
    [
        (literal_column(":case = 'upper'"), func.upper(colexpr))
    ], else_=func.lower(colexpr)
)

print(expr)
```

@zzzeek Thanks for the feedback. Before opening this issue I had tried what you suggested (to use `literal_column` instead of `text`), but I got the following error:

```
  File "/Users/denisahearn/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/sqlalchemy-bug-xulG5YFe-py3.7/lib/python3.7/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 2024, in _handle_dbapi_exception
    sqlalchemy_exception, with_traceback=exc_info[2], from_=e
  File "/Users/denisahearn/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/sqlalchemy-bug-xulG5YFe-py3.7/lib/python3.7/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/compat.py", line 207, in raise_
    raise exception
  File "/Users/denisahearn/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/sqlalchemy-bug-xulG5YFe-py3.7/lib/python3.7/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 1800, in _execute_context
    cursor, statement, parameters, context
  File "/Users/denisahearn/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/sqlalchemy-bug-xulG5YFe-py3.7/lib/python3.7/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/default.py", line 717, in do_execute
    cursor.execute(statement, parameters)
sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg2.errors.SyntaxError) syntax error at or near ":"
LINE 1: SELECT widgets.id AS widgets_id, CASE WHEN :case = 'upper' T...
                                                   ^

[SQL: SELECT widgets.id AS widgets_id, CASE WHEN :case = 'upper' THEN upper(widgets.name) ELSE lower(widgets.name) END AS widgets_name, widgets."case" AS widgets_case
FROM widgets
WHERE widgets.id = %(id_1)s]
[parameters: {'id_1': 1}]
(Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/14/f405)
```

My understanding is that the `text` function is necessary here because of the use of the `case` bind parameter. If `text` is no longer supported with how I'm trying to use it (it was supported in 1.3), is there a replacement I can use which works with bind parameters?

Thanks.

Hi,

I think you may replace it with
```py
case(
            [
                (sa.bindparam('case') == 'upper'), func.upper(colexpr))
            ],
            else_=func.lower(colexpr)
)
```

but I'm not 100% sure it will work

@CaselIT `bindparam` did indeed work for us, thanks so much for the suggestion!

One suggestion - it would be nice if the [documentation](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/sqlelement.html?highlight=case#sqlalchemy.sql.expression.case) for the `case` method showed an example with a bind parameter using `bindparam`. Had there been an example like this I think I may have been able to find this solution myself. Might save the next developer a little time.
If you want to try opening a pr i think it would be appreciated!

rename.from: TypeDecorator column_expression works in 1.3.x, raises ArgumentError in 1.4.x
rename.to: have text() be part of ExpressionElementRole

body: `select()` accepts `text()` in the columns clause, so text() should work in any expression element role location as there is no other way to have a textual phrase with bound parameters inside of it.

rename.from: have text() be part of ExpressionElementRole
rename.to: repair unusual ColumnArgumentRole used in case(), this is only meant for ORM cases

body: nevermind, it is actually the wrong role used in exactly this one place inside of case() for some reason, a regression indeed.
it looks like it's trying to guard against some other kind of input taht otherwise becomes a bound parameter.  but i think we just have to open it up again.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**use ExpressionElementRole for case targets in case()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3269

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_4** branch:

**use ExpressionElementRole for case targets in case()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3270
